description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three measures of accuracy—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for a model, likely an LLM, as referenced in the paper “Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback.” The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans a linear scale from 0.86 to 1.00, with tick labels appearing at intervals of 0.02. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 on a linear scale. The “Final Accuracy” is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers, remaining consistently high across the entire range of initial confidence, starting at approximately 0.95 and ending near 0.98. The “Δ Accuracy,” shown as a dashed orange line with diamond markers, begins at approximately 0.25, declines to a low of about 0.05 near initial confidence 0.95, then slightly recovers to about 0.20 near 1.00. The “Initial Accuracy,” depicted as a dashed green line with square markers, starts at approximately 0.65, rises to a peak of about 0.90 near initial confidence 0.97, then declines slightly to around 0.75 at the end of the range. All lines are accompanied by error bars indicating variability.
